paper.title: Geometric de-noising of protein-protein interaction networks
paper.citation: Kuchaiev O, Rašajski M, Higham DJ, Pržulj N. Geometric de-noising of protein-protein interaction networks. PLoS Comput Biol 5(8):e1000454 (2009)

skill.name: paper2repro
skill.note: The skill text loaded in the reproduction session (2026-11-09) matches the skill folder tagged paper2repro-v0.4.0; the installed skill was at this commit.

settings.what: Path lengths up to 29, unreachable pairs at 200, the diagonal at 2, each axis scaled to [0, 1], P(edge) = 0.001, 18,000 training distances, EM stop at a log-likelihood change below 0.01
settings.sensitivity: Not in the paper; read from the authors' embed_novi.m, assign_scores.m and EM.m and their web page (Wayback Machine). The port check runs embed_novi.m itself.

low_confidence.what: Collins et al.'s low-confidence edges are the pairs with 1.85 <= PE < 3.19 between Yhigh proteins (5,356 pairs)
low_confidence.sensitivity: The paper's (TP, FP) labels imply about 5,296 positives; Collins et al. clustered pairs down to PE 1.85. With a cut of 1.86 (5,297 pairs) the labelled TP counts fall by about 1% (output/run/fig2_label_hypotheses.json).

eps_grid.what: The markers sit at epsilon 0.01 to 0.1 in steps of 0.01 and 0.2 to 1.4 in steps of 0.1 (Figs 2, 3); 0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.1 to 0.5 and (1, 1) (Fig. 4); 0.01 to 0.05 in steps of 0.01, 0.1 to 0.5 and (1, 1) (Fig. 5, whose 1,000 and 2,000 curves show five markers below 2% false positives)
eps_grid.sensitivity: Only where the smoothed line bends between markers; the dense ROC (output/roc_dense.csv) gives the same AUC to 0.001.

excel_smoothing.what: Excel's smoothed line is drawn as a Catmull-Rom (tension 1/6) Bezier curve through the markers
excel_smoothing.sensitivity: Affects the line between markers only.

em_seed.what: The training sample and the EM start use our seed 2009 (the authors' Matlab used rand without a fixed state)
em_seed.sensitivity: Over 20 seeds HumanBG gives 1,679 to 2,361 pairs with CS >= 0.975 (output/human.json, runs).

fig5_dimension.what: Fig. 5 is drawn in the dimension that scores best of 4, 5 and 7 (dimension 5)
fig5_dimension.sensitivity: The other two dimensions are near-miss controls; their scores are in the item.

fig5_repeats.what: Fig. 5 draws the mean of 10 random deletions per size; the paper does not say how many it ran
fig5_repeats.sensitivity: AUC ranges over the repeats are in output/figures.json (auc_range_over_repeats, auc_range_over_repeats_every_protein). Single deletions spread widely when every protein is embedded: the 3,000 curve scores 7% to 84% in dimension 5 (output/run/fig5_single_deletions.json).

goa.what: GO annotations from GOA human release 70 (February 2009), direct annotations by symbol, NOT annotations dropped
goa.sensitivity: Releases 67-74 give 6,284 to 6,391 annotated proteins against the paper's 6,278. Release 70 is closest on the pairs sharing a term (7,428,577 against 7,400,424) and among the closest on proteins (6,292; release 74 has 6,284 but 7,496,814 pairs).

hprd.what: HPRD release 9 (April 2010, Pathway Commons 2 v3) stands in for the unnamed 2009 release (34,119 interactions)
hprd.sensitivity: A later release adds and drops pairs: on the paper's own 251 pairs it finds 11 against 12.

kegg.what: Current KEGG pathways stand in for the March 2009 release (205 human pathways; now 372)
kegg.sensitivity: The larger release finds more pairs in pathways.

fig5_embedding.what: Fig. 5's 500, 1,000 and 2,000 curves embed the largest component of what is left after the deletion; its 3,000 curve embeds every protein, including those the deletion cut off (embed_novi.m puts unreachable pairs at path length 200)
fig5_embedding.sensitivity: Only the 3,000 curve changes: its score rises from 33.1% to 40.4% and its AUC falls from 0.950-0.960 to 0.882-0.909, around the published 0.90. Drawing all four curves either way is a near-miss control (output/figures.json: series_scores_all_lcc, series_scores_all_whole).

fig5.label: Fig. 5, ROC for recovering 500 to 3,000 deleted Yhigh edges

cause.summary: The 3,000-edge curve was drawn from an embedding of every protein, cut-off ones included, while the 500 to 2,000 curves match an embedding of the largest component. The paper does not say this. Drawn that way, our 3,000 curve takes the published shape: it starts at sensitivity 0.45 at the first marker and levels off at 0.97. Its AUC (0.88 to 0.91 over 10 deletions) brackets the published 0.90. It still lies to the right of the published curve (40% within 2 px), because the paper drew one deletion and how far the cut-off proteins squeeze the rest varies from deletion to deletion. The 500, 1,000 and 2,000 curves are unchanged and lie close to the published ones (70.5%, 45.2% and 75.3% within 2 px).

page.lede: The authors' Matlab and the yeast test data were not lost after all: both turned up in web archives. We rebuilt the method in Python, checked it against their code, and ran every experiment again. Of {items} results, {exact} came back exactly, {agrees} agree, {partly} partly agree, {inconclusive} cannot be told apart, {differs} differ and {not_attempted} were not attempted.
page.items_caption: Every figure, table and number of the paper, in the paper's order. Paper and ours are both shown; the verdict is computed from them.
page.claims_line: The paper's main claim holds: the embedding recovers Collins' low-confidence yeast edges with AUC 0.93 and finds the human predictions of Table S1 (247 of 251). Some counts differ; the causes are the random EM fit behind the 0.975 cut, the later GO, HPRD and KEGG releases, and copies of the yeast data that differ from the paper's by a few edges.
came_back: embed_novi.m, assign_scores.m and EM.m were on the Wayback Machine (kuchaev.com/Denoising, 2016). They hold the settings the paper leaves out: path lengths up to 29, unreachable pairs at 200, each axis rescaled to [0, 1], P(edge) = 0.001.
Collins et al.'s PE scores for all 401,820 pairs were on the Wayback Machine too (interactome-cmp.ucsf.edu, 2010). PE >= 3.19 gives Yhigh with the paper's 1,004 proteins.
Pairs with 1.85 <= PE < 3.19, the cut Collins et al. used for clustering, give ROC curves on the published markers (Fig. 2); the labelled counts are 0.1% to 5.4% off.
The markers of Fig. 2 sit at epsilon 0.01 to 0.1 and 0.2 to 1.4; our points at the same epsilons land on them.

It is lower because that run embedded every protein, including those the deletion cut off: they sit at the unreachable distance, the per-axis scaling squeezes everything else, and the curve starts high and levels off at 0.97 as published. The 500 to 2,000 curves match the largest component.
Re-embedding with the predictions added converges in 6 to 14 rounds (the paper says about 10) and costs a little accuracy, as in Fig. 4.
BioGRID 2.0.35 keyed by upper-cased symbol: 7,514 proteins and 23,378 edges in the largest component (paper 7,513 and 23,372), and 2,837 edges further apart than 0.4 (paper 2,838).
buried: The paper's exact copy of the Collins high-confidence set (9,074 edges; the web copy has 9,070, BioGRID's 9,064)
The random training sample and EM start behind the 0.975 cut (1,685 pairs; ours range from 1,679 to 2,361 over 20 seeds)
The HPRD release of 2009 and KEGG of March 2009
Which deletion Fig. 5 drew for each size (its 3,000 curve keeps the proteins the deletion cut off, the others do not)
The p-values of Text S1: they do not follow from its own parameters (7.5e-8 should read 7.5e-16; the GO values are 3.4e-13 and 6.2e-27)
page.matched_intro: Where the inputs are the paper's own, the numbers come back.
matched: The Yhigh densities overlay the published curves (spike at 0, peak at 0.1, non-edge mode at 0.77).
Six ROC curves on the published grid; AUC 0.93 at dimension 7.
Both curves on the published markers.
247 of the 251 published pairs are among our high-confidence predictions; the other 4 involve proteins our HumanBG lacks.
The paper's own 251 pairs give 5 matches in BioGRID 2.0.50, as printed.
page.closing: Dug up from two web archives in November 2026: the authors' Matlab, Collins et al.'s scores, and every experiment of the paper rerun.
